Image URL: https://img.theepochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2014/10/08/456679188-1080x720.jpg# China Open 2014 Women’s Singles Final Ceremony

Maria Sharapova and Petra Kvitova posed together on the court at the China National Tennis Center in Beijing after the Women’s Singles Final on October 5, 2014. Sharapova, the champion, held the ornate gold trophy cup, while Kvitova displayed the silver runner-up plate. Both athletes wore their tennis attire—Sharapova in a white top and light blue skirt, Kvitova in a blue and white jacket and navy skirt—and stood in front of a line of ball kids and officials dressed in red and blue uniforms.

The China Open was part of the Asian Tennis Swing Tour, featuring top WTA players competing for ranking points and prize money. This final marked Sharapova’s first China Open title and her fifth tournament win of the year, earning her 1000 ranking points and nearly one million dollars in prize money. The event also served as a lead-up to the WTA Finals in Singapore, with both players having won Grand Slam titles earlier that season.

Image URL: https://s2.elespanol.com/2015/10/11/deportes/tenis/deportes-tenis_70752945_44060_854x640.jpg# Muguruza’s China Open Triumph

Garbiñe Muguruza poses proudly with the ornate gold trophy after defeating Timea Bacsinszky 7-5, 6-4 in the 2015 China Open final. Wearing a black-and-white Adidas dress and white visor, she celebrates her second WTA title on the blue court in Beijing.

At just 22, the Spanish-Venezuelan star overcame earlier injuries and tough matches against Lucic-Baroni and Agnieszka Radwanska to claim the championship. This victory propelled her to fourth in the WTA rankings, just one point shy of Maria Sharapova, highlighting her rapid ascent and mental fortitude in professional tennis.

Image URL: https://images.indianexpress.com/2016/10/agnieszka-radwanska-m.jpg# Radwanska’s China Open Triumph

Agnieszka Radwanska clinched the China Open women’s singles title in Beijing with a commanding 6-4, 6-2 victory over Johanna Konta. The Polish star broke Konta early in the first set, weathered a brief counterbreak, and then sealed the opener before dominating the second set with two more breaks and an ace to serve out the match.

This win marked Radwanska’s 20th career title and her third of the 2016 season, achieved without dropping a set throughout the tournament. The victory also echoed her previous success at the Beijing event in 2011. Konta’s run to the final secured her a spot in the WTA top-10 rankings, making her the first British woman to reach that milestone since 1984.

On court, Radwanska held the ornate gold trophy inscribed “Women’s Singles Champion,” her expression a mix of relief and pride. The bright red and gold of the trophy contrasted with her black athletic attire, capturing the celebratory mood of the final in early October.

Victoria Azarenka overcame a first-set loss to defeat Serena Williams 2-6, 6-2, 7-6 (8-6) in the 2013 Cincinnati WTA final. The two-hour-and-thirty-minute match featured powerful groundstrokes, strategic breaks of serve, and a tense deciding tie-break. Azarenka’s comeback in the second set and her composure in the final tie-break secured her third title of the year and the 17th of her career.

Both players delivered high-quality tennis, trading breaks and showcasing their top-ranked rivalry. Williams, seeking her first Cincinnati title, pushed Azarenka to the limit but ultimately saw her forehand drift wide in the final point. The victory highlighted Azarenka’s resilience and added a prestigious WTA crown to her growing list of achievements.

Serena Williams clinched her first Western & Southern Open title in Cincinnati on August 17, 2014, overcoming Ana Ivanovic 6-4, 6-1 in a commanding 62-minute performance. After dropping serve in the opening game, Williams rallied with powerful serving—delivering 12 aces—and capitalized on Ivanovic’s unforced errors to seize control of the match.

This victory ended Williams’ long quest for a Cincinnati crown, achieving the milestone on her sixth attempt and improving her finals record to 5-0 for the year. The win also highlighted her resilience, as she recovered from a stiff back and early break to dominate the final. Later that day, Roger Federer added to the tournament’s history by claiming his sixth Cincinnati title.

Caroline Wozniacki secured her 13th career championship at the Dubai Open on 20 February 2011, defeating Svetlana Kuznetsova in straight sets, 6-1, 6-3. The match lasted just 75 minutes, during which Wozniacki broke serve early in both sets and showcased her trademark movement and tactical prowess. Despite brief lapses in each set, she maintained psychological dominance and capitalized on Kuznetsova’s unforced errors.

The victory marked Wozniacki’s return to the world number one ranking after her Australian Open semi-final loss. She described the win as a confidence booster and emphasized her commitment to hard work and seizing opportunities. Kuznetsova, meanwhile, reflected on the importance of perspective beyond tennis, noting that life’s true priorities lie in health and family rather than rankings or prize money.
